press_blue.description: Blue colour key (BlueColour on the wire).

press_exit.description: Exit the current menu or app overlay.

press_green.description: Green colour key (GreenColour on the wire).

press_home.description: Open the home screen / smart-TV launcher.

press_info.description: Info banner for the current programme or item.

press_online.description: Open the online/smart-TV portal (older smart models).

press_options.description: Context options for the focused item.

press_play_pause.description: Play/pause toggle; same as Play on Android models.

press_power_off.description: Power off; maps to Standby on Android models (Home Assistant docs).

press_power_on.description: Power on — only while the TV still answers the network (warm standby); otherwise Wake-on-LAN is the documented route.

press_red.description: Red colour key (RedColour on the wire).

api_version.description: URL prefix matching the TV's api_version.Major from the System Probe — 1 on 2k9-2k13, 5 on 2014-2015 non-Android, 6 on Android/Saphi.

press_teletext.description: Open teletext (models/regions that still ship it).

press_tv_guide.description: Open the EPG (TvGuide on the wire).

press_viewmode.description: Cycle picture format (wide zoom, 4:3, ...) — Viewmode on the wire.

press_watch_tv.description: Switch to the broadcast tuner (WatchTV on the wire).

press_yellow.description: Yellow colour key (YellowColour on the wire).

set_power_standby.description: Put the TV in standby through the powerstate resource rather than a key code — the same endpoint the Power State sensor reads, written instead of read (spec-evolution P13 bound this; the endpoint itself was documented under http_endpoints all along). v6 only, like the read, and "support varies by firmware" even there — so this is NOT a fallback for sets that ignore the PowerOff key: those are the older sets, which have no powerstate resource at all. It is the off for a v6 set that answers powerstate but does not honour the key, and an explicit state request rather than a keypress whose effect depends on the model's key map.

device.name: Philips jointSPACE TV API
device.notes: Philips TVs expose a local REST-style JSON API whose URL prefix is the API major version: /1 on 2009-2013 jointSPACE models (some require one-time activation, see device.setup), /5 on 2014-2015 non-Android models, /6 on Android TVs (2014+) and Saphi/Linux sets. Two access regimes exist and the TV itself says which applies: GET /6/system returns featuring.systemfeatures with secured_transport and pairing_type. When secured_transport is true (2016+ Android) the API moves to HTTPS on port 1926 with a self-signed certificate and every request — GETs included — needs HTTP digest auth with credentials obtained from the on-screen PIN pairing flow (jointspace_common.auth). Otherwise the API is plain HTTP on port 1925 with no authentication at all. On Android models a bare GET /system (no version prefix) answers on both ports and is the probe every client uses to learn api_version.Major before picking a prefix. POSTs carry JSON bodies ({"key": "Home"}); there is no path-encoded command form like Roku's. See jointspace_common.transport_gaps for what that means for empty-body-only HTTP clients.

openness.notes: Philips published the v1 JSON API documentation and shipped the same docs on the TV itself (http://<ip>:1925/1/doc/), which earns this a documented_api status — but only for v1. API versions 5 and 6, the pairing flow, and the digest-auth regime were never officially published; they were recovered by suborb (2016, pairing), pylips (MITM of the official Philips remote app, v6 endpoint reference) and the haphilipsjs/Home Assistant authors. reverse_engineered is therefore true: half of this file is citation, half reconstruction.

upstream_docs.covers: The jointSPACE programme itself: supported model years (2k9 9000 range onward, xxPFL5xx6-xxPFL9xx6 for the 2k11 JSON API), the one-time activation digit sequence 5646877223, and the port-1925 entry point. Philips took the live site down; the archived copy is the authoritative remnant.

upstream_docs.covers: The official v1 method catalogue: ambilight/*, audio/volume, channellists, channels (+/current), input/key, sources (+/current) and system/*. v1 only — Philips never published the v5/v6 documentation; the versioned extensions below are reconstructed from client implementations.

issued_to_client: Digest-auth username (the client-chosen device id) and password (the TV-issued auth_key), from the pairing flow in jointspace_common.auth
credentials.notes: The WiFi passphrase is typed on the TV's own screen and never crosses a provisioning link this spec documents. API access control is the pairing flow, and it is all-or-nothing per model: pre-2016 models (secured_transport absent or false) accept every LAN client with no credentials at all — network reachability is the entire access control model, same caveat as Roku ECP. 2016+ Android models answer 401 to everything, including /system over HTTPS, until the client presents digest credentials from pairing; the TV shows the PIN and the user transcribes it, so pairing cannot be fully automated.
stored_on_device: Per-client pairing credentials (auth_key per paired device id)

factory_reset.effect: Clears channel lists, picture/sound and network settings, installed-app data and paired-client credentials; the TV returns to the first-time installation wizard.

steps.action: Settings > General settings > Factory settings (or 'Reinstall TV' on Android models), confirm on screen.
steps.notes: Menu wording varies by model year; both paths are documented in Philips' own user manuals. Public-source procedure, not run by this project.

methods.description: First-time installation on the TV itself: language, country, network selection and passphrase entry with the on-screen keyboard, channel scan. The wizard is driven with the bundled remote; no client participates.

steps.action: Power on the TV and complete the on-screen installation with the remote.
Select the WiFi network (or connect Ethernet) and enter the passphrase on the TV itself.
steps.expect: TV reports a network connection and shows its IP under network settings.

steps.action: On 2k9-2k11 models only: type 5646877223 on the remote while watching TV to activate the jointSPACE JSON API (one-time).
steps.notes: Not needed on 2014+ models; the API is always on there.

steps.action: Confirm the API is reachable and learn its version.
steps.expect: JSON with api_version.Major (1, 5 or 6) and, on v6, featuring.systemfeatures.secured_transport / pairing_type.

request.action: GET /system on port 1925, then GET /system on https port 1926 if 1925 does not answer

setup.notes: Network onboarding happens on the TV's own screen (first-time installation wizard); there is no app-driven provisioning protocol to reimplement. The API itself needs no enabling on 2014+ models. On the original 2k9/2k10/2k11 jointSPACE models the JSON API is off until a one-time activation: while watching TV, type 5646877223 on the remote ("jointspace" in multitap digit entry), per the jointSPACE project page. Separately from onboarding, 2016+ Android models require each client to PAIR once (on-screen PIN, jointspace_common.auth) before any request is accepted — that is credential issuance, not provisioning, so it lives in credentials below and in jointspace_common, not in methods.

rejoin.notes: The network settings menu re-runs only the network step; a factory reset is never needed just to change routers. Pairing credentials survive a network change — they are issued per client, not per network.

characteristics: API v1 on http port 1925, no auth; requires the 5646877223 activation sequence.
Endpoint set per the official v1 reference: system, sources, channels, channellists, audio, ambilight, input/key.
variants.name: Original jointSPACE models

characteristics: API v5 on http port 1925, no auth. Largely the v6 endpoint surface without activities/applications; pylips reports most v6 commands working on v5.
variants.name: API v5 models

characteristics: API v6. Reported (marcelrv gist, openHAB forums) to answer on http port 1925 without the digest-auth pairing of later Android sets; treat auth requirements as per-device, decided by featuring.systemfeatures.
variants.name: Early Android models

characteristics: API v6 on https port 1926, digest-auth pairing required (pairing_type: digest_auth_pairing, secured_transport: true). Port 1925 answers /system only, per community reports.
notifychange long-poll, channeldb channel lists, applications/activities, recordings and the settings-tree menuitems endpoints.
variants.name: Secured Android models

characteristics: API v6 reported by haphilipsjs with os_type 'Linux'; no Android intent activities, no applications listing, no source detect (Home Assistant feature matrix). Pairing behaviour follows systemfeatures as on Android.
variants.name: Non-Android v6 models

entities.name: Power
entities.notes: powerstate "On" when on, "Standby" otherwise. turn_off binds the PowerOff key, which maps to Standby on Android; key availability varies by model, and the one key every model takes is Standby — bound here as the toggle, so a consumer that has read the state has a universal off even where PowerOff is ignored. set_power_standby is the other discrete off, but it is v6-only and so narrower in reach than the key, not a fallback for the sets that ignore it. turn_on only reaches a TV still listening on the network — Wake-on-LAN is the documented route otherwise.

entities.name: Power On
entities.notes: Only reaches a TV still listening on the network; see commands.press_power_on.

entities.name: Power Off
entities.notes: Maps to Standby on Android models.

entities.name: Play/Pause
entities.notes: Same as Play on Android models.

entities.name: Source
entities.notes: Opens the input list; direct input switching is v1-only (sources/current) or a SELECTURI intent on v6 — see the Launch Application endpoint.

entities.name: Power State
entities.notes: v6 only, and absent on some firmwares; JSON {"powerstate": "On"}.

entities.name: Volume
entities.notes: JSON {min, max, current, muted}; device-scale integers, not percent.

entities.name: Current Channel
entities.notes: v5+; channel.name plus ccid. On v1 the path is /1/channels/current.

entities.name: Current Application
entities.notes: v6 Android only; an intent object. Broadcast TV reports the PlayTvActivity component, not null.

http_endpoints.description: Unversioned identity/version probe. Home Assistant's documented check: try http://<ip>:1925/system, then https://<ip>:1926/system; the answer carries api_version.Major/Minor/Patch, the TV's display name, the *_encrypted identity fields, and featuring.systemfeatures with secured_transport and pairing_type — everything a client needs to pick scheme, port, prefix and auth regime. On 2016+ Android models this is reported to be the only endpoint port 1925 still answers.
http_endpoints.name: System Probe

fields.description: Major/Minor/Patch; Major selects the URL prefix (1, 5 or 6).
fields.name: api_version

fields.description: systemfeatures.secured_transport / pairing_type decide the auth regime; jsonfeatures enumerates optional endpoint groups (ambilight, recordings, menuitems, applications, activities).
fields.name: featuring

http_endpoints.description: The versioned spelling of the same document; individual fields are also GETtable as /{api_version}/system/name, /system/country, /system/model, /system/serialnumber, /system/softwareversion (official v1 reference).
http_endpoints.name: System Info

http_endpoints.description: Press and release one remote key; the entire remote-control surface of the API. The full vocabulary, union of the official v1 reference, the pylips v6-tested list and the Home Assistant remote entity: Standby, PowerOn, PowerOff, CursorUp, CursorDown, CursorLeft, CursorRight, Confirm, Back, Exit, Home, Options, Adjust, Find, WatchTV, Source, List, Viewmode, TvGuide, Info, Subtitle, Teletext, ClosedCaption, RedColour, GreenColour, YellowColour, BlueColour, WhiteColour, Digit0 through Digit9, Dot, Next, Previous, ChannelStepUp, ChannelStepDown, VolumeUp, VolumeDown, Mute, HeadphonesVolume, Play, Pause, PlayPause, Stop, FastForward, Rewind, Record, Online, SmartTV, PhilipsMenu, Setup, AmbilightOnOff, PictureStyle, SoundStyle, SurroundMode, 3dFormat, 3dDepth, 2PlayerGaming, Multiview. Availability varies by model and year; PlayPause maps to Play and PowerOff to Standby on Android (Home Assistant docs). haphilipsjs also sends {"unicode": "<char>"} here for text entry. Long-press has no keydown/keyup split — unlike Roku, one POST is one complete press.
http_endpoints.name: Send Key

fields.description: One key name from the vocabulary above.
fields.name: key

fields.description: A literal character for text-entry fields (alternative to key).
fields.name: unicode

http_endpoints.description: Current volume and mute state.
http_endpoints.name: Volume State

http_endpoints.description: Set absolute volume and/or mute. Values are device-scale integers between the min/max the GET returned, not percent.
http_endpoints.name: Set Volume

http_endpoints.description: Current power state (v6; absent on some firmwares — haphilipsjs treats a 403/404 here as endpoint-not-present). Note a TV in standby stops answering the API entirely on many models (the jointSPACE docs already warn the API dies in standby); power-ON over the network is Wake-on-LAN or, on some Android sets, POST powerstate {"powerstate": "On"} — Home Assistant marks power-on "Yes (if always on)".
http_endpoints.name: Power State

http_endpoints.description: Request On/Standby/StandbyKeep/Reboot by name; support varies by firmware (v6).
http_endpoints.name: Set Power State

http_endpoints.description: Panel on/off independently of power (v5+).
http_endpoints.name: Screen State

http_endpoints.description: The channel-list index (v5+): the always-present virtual list "all" plus the favourite lists. Fetch a list's channels from channeldb/tv/channelLists/{id}; favourites from channeldb/tv/favoriteLists/{id}.
http_endpoints.name: Channel Database

http_endpoints.description: One channel list's channels (v5+); "all" enumerates everything tuned. Each channel carries a numeric ccid — the value Set Channel takes — plus name and preset. Some firmwares emit the malformed channelList fragment noted in jointspace_common.response_format.
http_endpoints.name: Channel List

http_endpoints.description: The tuned channel and its list, as the TV reports it (v5+; the v1 spelling is GET /1/channels/current with an id instead of a ccid).
http_endpoints.name: Current Channel

http_endpoints.description: Tune to a channel by ccid from a channel list (v5+; v1 spells it POST /1/channels/current with {"id": ...}).
http_endpoints.name: Set Channel

http_endpoints.description: Launchable apps with their Android intents (v6, Android models; jsonfeatures must list "applications"). Each entry's id is "<className>-<packageName>" and its intent object is exactly what Launch Application replays.
http_endpoints.name: Installed Applications

http_endpoints.description: The foreground activity as an intent object (v6, Android). Watching broadcast TV reports the PlayTvActivity component rather than a channel-free null.
http_endpoints.name: Current Application

http_endpoints.description: Launch an app by replaying the intent object from Installed Applications (v6, Android; jsonfeatures activities must include "intent"). The same mechanism switches inputs: an intent with action org.droidtv.playtv.SELECTURI and extras.uri of content://android.media.tv/passthrough/<input service> selects an HDMI input on sets whose firmware honours it — haphilipsjs hardcodes the MediaTek HW5-HW8 service names for HDMI 1-4. The Source key is the fallback where intents are refused.
http_endpoints.name: Launch Application

http_endpoints.description: Available inputs with ids (v1 only; removed from the API on v5/v6, where input switching is the Source key or a SELECTURI intent).
http_endpoints.name: Source List

http_endpoints.description: Switch input by id from Source List (v1 only, official v1 reference).
http_endpoints.name: Set Source

http_endpoints.description: Begin pairing; no auth. TV answers with timestamp + auth_key and shows the PIN. Full flow: jointspace_common.auth.pairing_flow. (v6 secured models.)
http_endpoints.name: Pairing Request

http_endpoints.description: Complete pairing with the on-screen PIN and the HMAC signature; digest auth (device id / auth_key) starts on this request. (v6 secured models.)
http_endpoints.name: Pairing Grant

http_endpoints.description: Long-poll state push: POST the last-known state map, the TV holds the connection and answers with only the changed subtrees (v6 models whose system advertises notifyChange). See jointspace_common.response_format.notifychange.
http_endpoints.name: Notify Change

http_endpoints.description: Ambilight control mode: internal (TV drives it), manual, expert, or lounge on models with LoungeLight (per the official v1 reference and haphilipsjs). POST the same path with {"current": "<mode>"} to change it; Android/Saphi firmwares have known mode-reporting quirks documented in haphilipsjs.
http_endpoints.name: Ambilight Mode

http_endpoints.description: Ambilight on/off state as {"power": "On"|"Off"} (v5+); POST the same path with {"power": ...} to set. On v1 the equivalent is ambilight/mode manual + a zeroed ambilight/cached write, per haphilipsjs.
http_endpoints.name: Ambilight Power

addressing.description: Base URL is <scheme>://<ip>:<port>/<api_version>/ where api_version is the Major field from the system probe (1, 5 or 6) and scheme/port are http/1925 or https/1926. Pre-Android models serve only http/1925. 2016+ Android models serve https/1926 and answer only the unversioned /system probe on http/1925, per community reports; haphilipsjs simply tries both protocols for "system" and follows whatever secured_transport says. The HTTPS certificate is self-signed — clients must skip verification or pin on first pairing; every published client disables verification.

pairing_flow.description: One-time per client, reverse engineered by suborb (2016) and carried verbatim by pylips and haphilipsjs. Note the wire paths are /6/pair/request and /6/pair/grant — frequently written "pairing/..." in secondary documentation, but every published client uses "pair/".
pairing_flow.shared_key: The HMAC key is a constant shipped in every client (it gates only the PIN signature, not transport security): base64 "ZmVay1EQVFOaZhwQ4Kv81ypLAZNczV9sG4KkseXWn1NEk6cXmPKO/MCa9sryslvLCFMnNe4Z4CPXzToowvhHvA==" (decode before use). The same key's first 16 bytes decrypt the *_encrypted system fields below.

steps.body: {"device": {"device_name": ..., "device_os": ..., "type": "native", "id": <client-chosen device id>, "app_id": ..., "app_name": ...}, plus the requested scope. haphilipsjs wraps the scope as "access": {"scope": ["read", "write", "control"], "featuring": <echo of /system's featuring>}; suborb's original sent a bare "scope": [...] sibling. Both are published working forms; the access-wrapped form is the maintained one.
steps.response: {"timestamp": <int>, "auth_key": "<string>", "timeout": ...} — and the TV displays a 4-digit PIN on screen. The user must read it and hand it to the client; this is the only human step.

steps.body: {"auth": {"auth_AppId": "1", "pin": "<the 4 digits>", "auth_timestamp": <timestamp from step 1>, "auth_signature": base64(HMAC-SHA1(shared_key, str(timestamp) + pin))}, "device": <same device object as step 1>}. Signature caveat: suborb's 2016 original base64-encoded the HMAC's HEX digest; haphilipsjs base64-encodes the raw 20-byte digest. haphilipsjs is the maintained implementation Home Assistant pairs with today, so its form is the reference; treat the other as historical.
steps.request: POST /6/pair/grant with digest auth (username = device id, password = auth_key)
steps.response: {"error_id": "SUCCESS"}. From this point the client sends digest auth (device id / auth_key) on every request. There is no token expiry in the published clients; the credentials work until the TV is reset or unpaired.

regimes.digest_auth_pairing: 2016+ Android models (pairing_type: "digest_auth_pairing", secured_transport: "true"): HTTPS on 1926, and EVERY request — including GET /6/system — is answered 401 without HTTP digest auth. Username is the client-chosen device id from pairing; password is the auth_key the TV issued. The TV forgets a client only on factory reset or an explicit unpair in its menus.
regimes.open: Pre-2016 models (no pairing_type, or secured_transport false in /{v}/system's featuring.systemfeatures): plain HTTP on 1925, no credentials of any kind. Anything on the LAN can drive the TV.

request_format.description: GETs have no body. POSTs carry a JSON object as the entire body with Content-Type application/json — {"key": "Home"} for a remote key, {"current": 20, "muted": false} for volume. There is no form encoding and no path-encoded command variant. In the `commands` block below, a command's `arguments` map IS that JSON object: the renderer substitutes parameters into it and serializes the result as the request body.

http.body: The command's arguments, serialized as one JSON object. Empty only for GETs.
http.headers: Content-Type: application/json on POSTs. Accept: application/json is what haphilipsjs sends. On secured models every request additionally carries an HTTP Digest Authorization header (see auth); on open models no headers beyond Content-Type are needed.

response_format.description: JSON, with real-world warts. Command POSTs answer 200 with an empty or near-empty body (haphilipsjs treats "", "OkOk", "}" and the literal "Context Service not started" as empty). Pairing answers carry "error_id": "SUCCESS" as a string. Booleans are frequently the strings "On"/"Off" or "true"/"false". 401 means the digest credentials are missing or wrong (secured models); haphilipsjs treats 403/404 as "this endpoint does not exist on this firmware" and caches it dead. Some firmwares emit malformed JSON — doubled commas, a dangling '"channelList": { "id": "version", "" }' fragment — which haphilipsjs repairs with string surgery before parsing; a strict parser will choke where a real TV is merely sloppy.
response_format.encrypted_fields: GET /{v}/system returns serialnumber, softwareversion, model and deviceid as <name>_encrypted strings: base64 of AES-128-CBC ciphertext with PKCS7 padding, where the key is bytes 0-15 of the base64-decoded shared key above and the IV is the first 16 bytes of the decoded payload. Decryption is how a client learns the serial for stable identity without pairing first (the system probe needs no auth on open models, and is the one GET some secured models answer on 1925).
response_format.notifychange: Models whose /6/system has notifyChange set (e.g. "http") support POST /6/notifychange: a long-poll whose request body is the client's last-known state map (activities/tv, audio/volume, powerstate, ...) and whose response — which can take over a minute — carries only what changed. TVs commonly close the idle connection; clients treat that as a retry, not a failure.

gaps.detail: Every POST on this API — all remote keys, volume, power, channel and source changes — takes a JSON object body. The app transport sends GET/POST with an empty body only, so not one command in this spec is executable by it yet. The `arguments` map on each command is the body, ready for a renderer that can send one.
2016+ models serve only https on 1926 with a cert no client can chain to a root. The client must skip verification (what every published client does) or TOFU-pin during pairing.

Secured models 401 everything without an Authorization header — GETs included. Pairing (itself one unauthenticated POST, one digest POST, plus a PIN the user reads off the TV screen) must run once before any endpoint in this file answers.
gaps.gap: HTTP digest auth on every request

gaps.detail: The `options_source`/`state_source` select contract parses XML element/attribute shapes. This API's option lists (channeldb channel lists, applications) are JSON arrays of objects, so a channel/app picker cannot be declared with the schema's current select machinery — documented here as endpoints instead.

transport_gaps.summary: What the reference mobile app's HTTP transport does NOT implement today, and which therefore stands between this spec and a working control. Recorded, not worked around: the commands below are written the way the TV expects them, and none of them is sendable by an empty-body, no-auth HTTP client.
